jobs.title: Agricultural Field Technician
jobs.description:
Amalgamated Sugar Company is looking for a Agriculture Field Technician working under the direction of our Chief Scientist – Senior Plant Pathologist, this role is focused on managing the day-to-day operations of the Amalgamated Sugar Company’s insectary and greenhouse (estimated 20-30 hrs./week), as well as supporting scientifically rigorous research trials in the field (estimated 10-20 hrs./week). You will be a part of a team dedicated to contributing new knowledge to sugarbeet growers in Idaho, Oregon, and Washington to enable them to improve their sugarbeet productivity, profitability, and sustainability. The role is ideally suited to someone who has an eye for detail, enjoys working in a greenhouse setting with insects, and has an inquisitive mind. Research conducted includes agronomy and farming system research trials, as well as the evaluation of new pesticides for the control of diseases, insects, and weeds. Based in Nyssa, OR, this position is with Amalgamated Sugar Company’s Sugarbeet Research (SBR) Team.

Primary Responsibilities

Insectary and Greenhouse Management

Manage day-to-day insectary and greenhouse operations with minimal supervision, prioritizing tasks to meet timelines.
Propagate, grow, and maintain sugarbeet plants to support insect colonies and experiments (e.g., seeding, transplanting, watering, fertilization, and sanitation).
Rear beet leafhoppers and maintain healthy colonies; produce and deliver adequate numbers of viruliferous leafhoppers for field trials according to established protocols.
Scout plants routinely for insects, mites, and diseases; implement integrated pest management (IPM) and apply pesticides as needed in accordance with label directions and all applicable state/federal requirements.
Maintain greenhouse and insectary infrastructure, including environmental controls, irrigation systems, lighting, benches, and insect containment features; perform and coordinate repairs and preventive maintenance as needed.
Monitor and document key environmental parameters (e.g., temperature, humidity, and photoperiod) and adjust settings to maintain consistent plant and insect performance.
Maintain cleanliness to prevent spread of pests or pathogens between experiments and growing areas.
Maintain accurate records for pesticide applications, and trial support activities.
Track and maintain inventory of plants, insects, growing supplies, and chemicals; coordinate ordering and proper storage/disposal in compliance with regulations.
Promote safe work practices in the greenhouse and insectary, including proper PPE use, chemical handling, and hazard reporting; recommend and implement improvements to safety procedures.

Field and Technical Support

Support the Chief Scientist – Senior Plant Pathologist and Research Agronomist in planning, organizing, and executing field and glasshouse research trials.
Assist with establishing experiments, including trial design support, plot layout and marking, planting/seeding, and accurate application of experimental treatments.
Perform routine cultural practices and plot maintenance (e.g., cultivation, thinning, fertilization support, replanting, and border management) to maintain trial integrity.
Manage day-to-day trial operations, including irrigation scheduling, crop scouting, and weed/insect/disease control; calibrate and operate application equipment and ensure treatments are applied safely and according to protocol and label requirements.
Collect research measurements and samples as assigned; follow protocols for sampling, labeling, handling, and storage to protect data quality and traceability.
Assist with harvest operations, including plot harvesting and collection of yield and quality data.
Enter, organize, and format trial data using Microsoft Excel; perform basic data checks to identify missing values, outliers, or inconsistencies.
Maintain accurate, timely records of trial activities (e.g., field operations, treatment applications, scouting observations, deviations, and equipment logs) in accordance with research documentation standards.
Assist with transporting research and farm equipment by road, including safe loading/unloading, securing loads, and trailering as needed.
Operate, clean, and perform routine maintenance on research equipment and small plot implements (e.g., planters, sprayers, pumps, and sensors) and report repair needs promptly.
Communicate progress and field observations (e.g., pest pressure, disease symptoms, stand issues, irrigation problems) and escalate urgent issues to project leads in a timely manner.
Coordinate day-to-day logistics for trial work, including staging supplies, preparing labels and datasheets, and assisting with training/oversight of seasonal staff when assigned.
Ensure field and glasshouse work is conducted safely (PPE, chemical safety, equipment operation, and heat/cold stress awareness) and contribute to continuous improvement of safe work practices.

Secondary RESPONSIBILITIES

Administrative Support

Assist with preparation of reports/information for publication and/or presentation to industry.
Assist with the design and development of innovative extension materials.
Assist with the preparation of the Sugarbeet Research Magazine.
Supervision of seasonal field staff as required

Essential Skills And Attributes

Interest in greenhouse work and entomology; comfort working around insects is essential.
Plant production and care skills (seeding, transplanting, watering, fertilization), insect rearing/handling, pesticide use, and operation of basic farm/greenhouse implements.
Valid driver’s license in Idaho or Oregon (or ability to obtain).
Current Idaho and Oregon pesticide applicator license(s), or willingness/ability to obtain both within 6 months of employment.
Idaho or Oregon Commercial Class A driver’s license (CDL), or willingness/ability to obtain within 6 months of employment.
Strong attention to detail and the ability to follow research protocols, treatment plans, and data-collection methods consistently.
Comfortable with accurate recordkeeping and documentation (e.g., pesticide application records, environmental logs, and trial notes).
Basic math and measurement skills for mixing, calibrating, and applying treatments and for collecting field/greenhouse data.
Mechanical aptitude and comfort operating, troubleshooting, and maintaining common greenhouse.
Ability to follow sanitation, containment, and biosecurity procedures to protect insect colonies and prevent cross-contamination between trials.
Proficiency with Microsoft Excel, Word, and PowerPoint; willingness to learn Adobe InDesign.
Highly organized with the ability to plan work, manage multiple projects, and meet deadlines with minimal supervision.
Commitment to workplace safety, including proper PPE, chemical safety, equipment safety, and proactive hazard identification and reporting.
Comfort performing hands-on work in greenhouse and outdoor conditions, including heat, cold, dust, and moisture.
Ability to travel for work, including occasional overnight stays.
Ability to work under time-sensitive conditions while maintaining a professional, steady approach.
High personal integrity, reliability, and a commitment to producing accurate, high-quality work.
Collaborative, team-oriented mindset; communicates effectively and builds positive working relationships internally and externally.

Minimum Education And Experience

A bachelor’s degree with an emphasis in agronomy, soil, or plant science is required.
Experience with greenhouse operations is required and with farm equipment is desirable.
The ability to obtain and maintain a ID/OR pesticide applicator license is required, and to obtain and maintain an Idaho or Oregon State Commercial Class A driver’s license (CDL) is desirable.
Knowledge of trial management or replicated small plot research is desirable
Preferred 2-4 years of work-related experience in the field;
OR any equivalent combination of experience and education which provides the required knowledge, skills, and abilities.

jobs.title: Environmental Scientist/Human Health Risk Assessor
jobs.description:
At Jacobs, we're challenging today to reinvent tomorrow by solving the world's most critical problems for thriving cities, resilient environments, mission-critical outcomes, operational advancement, scientific discovery and cutting-edge manufacturing, turning abstract ideas into realities that transform the world for good.

Your impact

When it comes to environmental consulting, we are focused on cleaning up our communities today to improve our tomorrow. Site environmental investigations and human health risk assessments rely on data analyses to accurately characterize and quantify exposures to and effects of environmental contaminants. Data-driven solutions are a key component of Jacobs’ overall strategy.

We are seeking a detail-oriented Environmental Scientist with strong quantitative skills to work on human health risk assessments for complex site characterization and remediation projects for both federal and private sector clients
.

Based anywhere in the United States, you will support human health risk assessments from study design to site characterization, data evaluation, and interpretation. You will gain experience with Remedial Investigation/Feasibility Study projects and how human health risk assessment fits into the overall environmental site closure process. Evaluations will include receptor exposure estimation/modeling, relating literature-based toxicity data for risk estimation, risk characterization, and overall reporting. You will interact with technical experts from multiple fields to develop and implement comprehensive site strategies and deliver innovative solutions on challenging sites. Under the supervision of mid-level and senior level risk assessors, you will work primarily on projects in the United States for clients including federal (USEPA, Department of Defense), mining and other industrial, and with contaminant classes including metals, polynuclear aromatic hydrocarbons and petroleum, chlorinated organics, pesticides, per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances, and more. The majority of your duties will be office-based, but you may be expected to travel to some project sites where you will participate in site characterization activities that can support human health risk assessments. Additionally, your duties can also include providing support to senior staff that communicates project results to clients and other stakeholders, including the regulatory community.

You will work in a flexible, supportive team environment with experienced staff who will mentor and assist you in your career growth at Jacobs, and who will also learn from the knowledge, experience, and perspectives you bring to Jacobs. Our global human health risk team is located across the US and in various countries, such as Canada, Europe, and Australia. You will be involved in multiple projects and must be effective at time management, prioritization of tasks, and clear communication with your project teams and clients. You may have opportunities to attend and participate in professional society conferences.

Jacobs delivers projects with high safety, compliance, and quality standards expected by both Jacobs and our clients. Our global team is here to provide you with the tools to keep your career growing as well as those around you. By driving consistency and innovation across site characterization and remediation projects, you will help your team achieve the clients’ goals. Bring your positive outlook and flexible leadership style, and we will help grow what drives you – solving complex site characterization and remediation problems, together.

At Jacobs, we are partnering across the globe to create the best project outcomes by maximizing the design, digital technology, and support capabilities of our Global Integrated Delivery (GID) teammates. By joining Jacobs, you will commit to supporting and engaging with these teams, as we work to build a company like no other.

Here's what you'll need

Bachelor’s or master’s degree in biology, toxicology, public health, environmental science or other closely related technical degree.
Software skills – Microsoft Office suite (Excel, Access, Word, PowerPoint) and statistical software
Open to occasional travel.
Strong attention to detail.
Ability to communicate verbally and in writing
Ability to think strategically and critically analyze details
Strong networking/self-promoting skills.
One to two years of professional experience preferred, preferably in consulting, working on biology, toxicology, and/or environmental science projects.

Our health and welfare benefits are designed to invest in you, and in the things you care about. Your health. Your well-being. Your security. Your future. Employees have access to medical, dental, vision, and basic life insurance, a 401(k) plan, and the ability to purchase company stock at a discount. Eligible employees may also enroll in a deferred compensation plan or the Executive Deferral Plan. Jacobs has an unlimited U.S. Personalized Paid Time Off (PPTO) policy for full-time salaried/exempt employees, seven paid holidays, and caregiver leave. And certain roles may be eligible for additional rewards, including merit increases, performance discretionary bonus, and stock.

The base salary range for this position is $70,900.00 to $97,500.00. Within the range, individual pay is determined by work location and additional factors, including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability or protected veteran status. Job posted on April 21, 2026. This position will be open for at least 3 days.

At Jacobs, we’re partnering across the globe to create the best project outcomes by maximizing the design, digital technology, and support capabilities of our Global Integrated Delivery (GID) teammates. By joining Jacobs, you’ll commit to supporting and engaging with these teams, as we work to build a company like no other.

We value collaboration and believe that in-person interactions are crucial for both our culture and client delivery. Job Details

Description

About Us: 

Meduit is a national leader in healthcare revenue cycle management, supporting hospitals and physician practices in 48 states. We focus on optimizing payments, allowing clients to focus on patient care, and pride ourselves on our core values: Integrity, Teamwork, Continuous Improvement, Client-Focused, and Results-Oriented. Learn more at www.meduitrcm.com. 

About the Role: 

The Data Analyst (Business Intelligence – Analytics Platform)
is responsible for owning and delivering analytics solutions that support operational and financial decision-making. This role ensures accuracy, usability, and reliability of data and analytics products. The Data Analyst partners with business, Data Engineering, BI, IT, and operational teams to develop scalable analytics solutions, define reporting requirements, and deliver actionable insights.

Title: Data Analyst (Business Intelligence)

Location: Remote

Department: Product Development

Reports To: Director of Analytics Engineering

Compensation: $80,000 and up, depending on qualifications

Key Responsibilities

Analyze datasets to identify trends, anomalies, and key business drivers
Collaborate with stakeholders to define reporting requirements, KPIs, and success metrics
Validate data logic, testing, and reconciliation across systems
Develop and maintain Power BI dashboards and reports
Write and optimize SQL queries and support ETL processes

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in data Analytics, Computer Science, Information Systems, Business Analytics, Statistics, or a related field
Experience with Snowflake and SQL environments
Strong SQL proficiency and analytical problem-solving skills
Experience with healthcare or Revenue Cycle Management (RCM) data
Experience with ETL processes and pipelines

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with Power BI
Experience with analytics platforms
Familiarity with data governance and security practices
Experience with Jira and GitHub

Employment Eligibility

Must be legally authorized to work in the United States without sponsorship

As a condition of employment, a pre-employment background check will be conducted

jobs.title: Data Analyst / Business Intelligence Developer
jobs.description:
The Actuarial Systems Data & Reporting team is looking for a Business Intelligence Analyst to help support US actuarial reporting, data analysis, and reporting modernization work. This role will work closely with the US Reporting Steward, Actuarial teams, and Global Systems & Data partners to understand business needs, investigate data issues, and deliver practical reporting solutions.

The work will include querying and analyzing data using SQL, Qlik, and Power BI; improving existing reports and controls; and helping build new solutions that support Quarter-end and Year-end valuation processes. The role will also help manage change requests by supporting intake, prioritization, tracking, and follow-up through JIRA.

Position Responsibilities

Technical (Data, Analytics, and Reporting)

Write, review, and optimize SQL queries to pull, transform, and validate large datasets from warehouse and data lake environments
Review Quarter-end and Year-end valuation data to identify trends, explain variances, and investigate data anomalies
Build and maintain data models that support QlikView and Power BI reporting
Create and improve dashboards used for reporting, reconciliations, and variance analysis
Validate and reconcile data across source systems, reporting layers, and downstream outputs
Help automate recurring data checks and controls to improve accuracy and reduce manual effort
Troubleshoot data issues by tracing logic across ETL steps, source data, and reporting dependencies
Support SIT and UAT by validating results, documenting findings, and confirming that business requirements are met
Document data lineage and source-to-target mappings so logic is clear, traceable, and audit-ready
Work with platforms such as Azure SQL, Data Lake, and Databricks as part of reporting and data analysis work
Use Python where helpful for analysis, automation, or repeatable data checks

Project / Change Management / Coordination

Work with business and technical teams to turn reporting needs into clear, actionable requirements
Help manage enhancement requests in JIRA, including intake, prioritization, tracking, and follow-up
Participate in Agile ceremonies such as backlog refinement, sprint planning, and status updates
Coordinate SIT and UAT activities with business users, developers, and other partners
Communicate data issues clearly, explain the impact, and help identify practical next steps
Support release readiness, deployment validation, and post-release checks
Look for opportunities to simplify reporting processes, reduce manual work, and improve controls
Keep documentation current for requirements, testing, decisions, and governance needs

Required Qualifications

Technical Skills & Experience

Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Finance, Mathematics, or a related field
2–5 years of hands-on experience writing SQL queries and working with large datasets

Overview

We are seeking a Data Analyst to support federal government trade, analytics, and mission transformation priorities by preparing, analyzing, documenting, and reporting on complex data to support data-driven decision-making. This role will support data science project teams by conducting data mining, data preparation, data quality review, reporting, needs and gaps assessments, and analytical studies across large and complex data environments.

The ideal candidate brings hands-on experience with data analysis, data preparation, reporting, database support, and visualization, along with the ability to work closely with data scientists, engineers, architects, project managers, and government stakeholders. This role requires an analyst who can assess the accuracy and reasonableness of data, support implementation of analytical models, document findings, and help transform data into clear, concise, and actionable insights.

Location

This role will primarily support work in the Washington, DC Metro area, with work expected at or near the client site in Ashburn, VA as required by the contract. Telework may be permitted only with prior government approval.

Security Requirement

U.S. Citizenship required due to federal contract requirements
Recent DHS Public Trust, DoD Secret, or DoD Top Secret clearance required

Four (4) years of relevant experience in applied research directed to machine learning, statistics, applied mathematics, data science, computer science, operations research, or another closely related quantitative or mathematical discipline
At least two (2) years of experience in applied data science research or big data analytics
Bachelor’s degree in Statistics, Applied Mathematics, Data Science, Computer Science, Operations Research, or another closely related scientific or technical discipline

Preferred Qualifications

Master’s degree in Statistics, Applied Mathematics, Data Science, Computer Science, Operations Research, Analytics, or another closely related discipline
Demonstrated knowledge of data mining methods, databases, data visualization, and machine learning
Ability to communicate analysis techniques, concepts, and products

Ability to develop data-driven analysis and reports based on data visualizations and data models
Experience supporting DHS, CBP, or other federal law enforcement, trade, revenue, regulatory, or mission operations environments

Experience working with high-volume structured and unstructured data from disparate sources, including transactional, entity, network, operational, or case management data
Experience using SQL, Python, R, Excel, SAS, Spark, Databricks, AWS, or similar tools for data preparation, analysis, reporting, or visualization
Experience with data profiling, data quality assessment, data cleansing, validation, reconciliation, and issue documentation
Experience developing dashboards, reports, data visualizations, or self-service analytics products using Tableau, Power BI, QuickSight, or similar platforms
Experience supporting machine learning, statistical modeling, anomaly detection, entity resolution, network analysis, cohort analysis, or risk-scoring projects
Experience writing analytical summaries, technical documentation, user guides, data dictionaries, or standard operating procedures
Experience working in Agile, Scrum, SAFe, or similar iterative delivery environments
Experience working in secure, compliant federal IT or data environments

Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to identify trends, anomalies, inconsistencies, and meaningful patterns in data
Strong communication skills with the ability to explain data findings, analytical concepts, and reporting products to technical and non-technical audiences
Detail-oriented with a focus on data accuracy, completeness, documentation, and quality
Ability to translate stakeholder questions and operational needs into practical data analyses, reports, and visualizations
Ability to manage multiple priorities and deliver high-quality work in an Agile environment
Collaborative and proactive with the ability to work effectively with data scientists, engineers, architects, developers, project managers, and end users

Position Title

Interviews:

Who We Are

Oregon Judicial Department (OJD) serves the public, and the people we serve may be facing challenging life circumstances, high levels of stress, or confusion about their next steps. The work you will do in this role affects members of our community who come to the court to have their cases resolved. We need people who want to impact their communities, value OJD’s efforts to remove barriers to access justice services, and welcome interacting with the public.

We are committed to building a diverse, inclusive team and encourage candidates of all backgrounds to apply. We consider relevant work experience, education, and any transferable skills and abilities that may meet our qualifications or the skills and attributes we need for this position. We welcome all candidates who are inspired by our work and mission.

Benefits To You

We pay 95% to 99% of medical insurance premiums for full-time employees [OR up to 99% of medical insurance premiums for part-time employees], including mental health coverage.
The hourly equivalent for this position is $38.69 - $60.02. [OR the annual salary for this position is $80,467 - $124,833.]
10 paid holidays, 2 floating holidays, 3 personal business days, separate sick and vacation paid leaves (prorated for part-time employees), and other employee benefits such as optional insurances and flexible spending plans.
OJD will pay you a 5% allowance for bilingual skills (includes ASL) if you can pass a skills test and are assigned to use those skills on the job!
Salary offers are made with consideration of the candidate’s education and experience.

Location Highlights

Portland, Oregon was founded in 1845 (incorporated in 1851). It is the state’s largest city and the county seat for Multnomah County. It is named for Portland, Maine. It is situated at the confluence of the Willamette and Columbia Rivers. Recreational activities include, numerous museums (including OMSI), parks (including Forest Park, largest wilderness park in city limits in the nation), hiking (including in-city hiking trails), restaurants (including Food Carts), Mt Hood (about 50 miles east) and much more. Portland is home to three major sports teams: Trailblazers (NBA), Timbers (MLS), and Thorns (NWSL).

Position Highlights

The Multnomah County Circuit Court is hiring a DUII Intensive Supervisor Program (DISP) Court Coordinator
(Program Coordinator).

In this role…

You will serve as the primary point of contact between the treatment court team: including the judge, prosecutors, defense counsel, probation officers, treatment providers, case manager, and peer mentors, and judicial staff ensuring integrated communication and cohesive operations.

Lead and manage regular staffing meetings and court sessions, preparing rosters and progress summaries to support informed decision-making.

Engage in evidence-based practices that are in alignment with the Oregon Specialty Court Standards, All Rise Best Practice Standards, and Ten Guiding Principles for DWI Courts.

Assist the team DDA with the screening process for eligible DUII court candidates which includes, providing risk assessments and collecting DUII court screening data for ongoing internal assessment regarding equitable and efficient referral and entry processes. Additionally, you will be involved with the department analyst for ongoing internal data tracking and internal evaluation processes.

Attend all team meetings and court events and use the court case management system (Odyssey) and the Treatment Court Case Management System (TCMS) to schedule the court’s dockets, produce and maintain all documentation related to the operation of the program, enter data reflecting the work of the court, and record case events for all court proceedings. You will gather information related to participant engagement and compliance with program directives through contact with case managers, community partners, or other public or private sector agencies and update Odyssey and TCMS. You will gather and maintain statistics critical to grant reporting and compliance. You will also monitor grant compliance, spending, and submission. You will maintain and update policy/procedure manuals and participant handbooks to ensure clarity and compliance with program standards.

Work collaboratively with the department analyst to conduct programmatic quality assurance, examining the effectiveness of services, and recommending adjustments to case management or treatment options. You will work with the team to ensure application of culturally competent practices and make programmatic adjustments / refinements based on individual participant needs.

Build and maintain strong collaborative partnerships with national and state treatment court training divisions (Impaired Driving Solutions (IDA), OSCA Treatment Court Team, Criminal Justice Commission (DCJ), Department of Community Justice (DCJ) Oregon Department of Transportation (ODOT), and Local Public Safety Council (LPSCC).

new_jobs.title: Environmental Scientist/Human Health Risk Assessor
new_jobs.description:
At Jacobs, we're challenging today to reinvent tomorrow by solving the world's most critical problems for thriving cities, resilient environments, mission-critical outcomes, operational advancement, scientific discovery and cutting-edge manufacturing, turning abstract ideas into realities that transform the world for good.

Your impact

When it comes to environmental consulting, we are focused on cleaning up our communities today to improve our tomorrow. Site environmental investigations and human health risk assessments rely on data analyses to accurately characterize and quantify exposures to and effects of environmental contaminants. Data-driven solutions are a key component of Jacobs’ overall strategy.

We are seeking a detail-oriented Environmental Scientist with strong quantitative skills to work on human health risk assessments for complex site characterization and remediation projects for both federal and private sector clients
.

Based anywhere in the United States, you will support human health risk assessments from study design to site characterization, data evaluation, and interpretation. You will gain experience with Remedial Investigation/Feasibility Study projects and how human health risk assessment fits into the overall environmental site closure process. Evaluations will include receptor exposure estimation/modeling, relating literature-based toxicity data for risk estimation, risk characterization, and overall reporting. You will interact with technical experts from multiple fields to develop and implement comprehensive site strategies and deliver innovative solutions on challenging sites. Under the supervision of mid-level and senior level risk assessors, you will work primarily on projects in the United States for clients including federal (USEPA, Department of Defense), mining and other industrial, and with contaminant classes including metals, polynuclear aromatic hydrocarbons and petroleum, chlorinated organics, pesticides, per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances, and more. The majority of your duties will be office-based, but you may be expected to travel to some project sites where you will participate in site characterization activities that can support human health risk assessments. Additionally, your duties can also include providing support to senior staff that communicates project results to clients and other stakeholders, including the regulatory community.

You will work in a flexible, supportive team environment with experienced staff who will mentor and assist you in your career growth at Jacobs, and who will also learn from the knowledge, experience, and perspectives you bring to Jacobs. Our global human health risk team is located across the US and in various countries, such as Canada, Europe, and Australia. You will be involved in multiple projects and must be effective at time management, prioritization of tasks, and clear communication with your project teams and clients. You may have opportunities to attend and participate in professional society conferences.

Jacobs delivers projects with high safety, compliance, and quality standards expected by both Jacobs and our clients. Our global team is here to provide you with the tools to keep your career growing as well as those around you. By driving consistency and innovation across site characterization and remediation projects, you will help your team achieve the clients’ goals. Bring your positive outlook and flexible leadership style, and we will help grow what drives you – solving complex site characterization and remediation problems, together.

At Jacobs, we are partnering across the globe to create the best project outcomes by maximizing the design, digital technology, and support capabilities of our Global Integrated Delivery (GID) teammates. By joining Jacobs, you will commit to supporting and engaging with these teams, as we work to build a company like no other.

Here's what you'll need

Bachelor’s or master’s degree in biology, toxicology, public health, environmental science or other closely related technical degree.
Software skills – Microsoft Office suite (Excel, Access, Word, PowerPoint) and statistical software
Open to occasional travel.
Strong attention to detail.
Ability to communicate verbally and in writing
Ability to think strategically and critically analyze details
Strong networking/self-promoting skills.
One to two years of professional experience preferred, preferably in consulting, working on biology, toxicology, and/or environmental science projects.

Our health and welfare benefits are designed to invest in you, and in the things you care about. Your health. Your well-being. Your security. Your future. Employees have access to medical, dental, vision, and basic life insurance, a 401(k) plan, and the ability to purchase company stock at a discount. Eligible employees may also enroll in a deferred compensation plan or the Executive Deferral Plan. Jacobs has an unlimited U.S. Personalized Paid Time Off (PPTO) policy for full-time salaried/exempt employees, seven paid holidays, and caregiver leave. And certain roles may be eligible for additional rewards, including merit increases, performance discretionary bonus, and stock.

The base salary range for this position is $70,900.00 to $97,500.00. Within the range, individual pay is determined by work location and additional factors, including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability or protected veteran status. Job posted on April 21, 2026. This position will be open for at least 3 days.

At Jacobs, we’re partnering across the globe to create the best project outcomes by maximizing the design, digital technology, and support capabilities of our Global Integrated Delivery (GID) teammates. By joining Jacobs, you’ll commit to supporting and engaging with these teams, as we work to build a company like no other.

We value collaboration and believe that in-person interactions are crucial for both our culture and client delivery. We empower employees with our hybrid working policy, allowing them to split their work week between Jacobs offices/projects and remote locations enabling them to deliver their best work.

Your application experience is important to us, and we’re keen to adapt to make every interaction even better. If you require further support or reasonable adjustments with regards to the recruitment process (for example, you require the application form in a different format), please contact the team via Careers Support.

new_jobs.description:
Requirements And Preferences

The Broward County Board of County Commissioners is seeking qualified candidates for the Natural Resources Specialist - (Environmental Field Inspector-Haz-Mat/Storage Tanks) to support the Environmental Permitting Division.

2026
Benefits of Broward County Employment

High Deductible Health Plan – Bi-weekly Premiums

Single $10.90 / Family $80.79

Includes a County Funded Health Savings Account of up to $2000 Annually

Consumer Driven Health Plan – Bi-weekly Premiums

Single $82.58 / Family $286.79

Florida Retirement System (FRS) – Pension or Investment Plan

457 Deferred Compensation Employee Match

Eleven (11) paid holidays each year

Vacation (Paid Time Off) = 2 weeks per year

Up to 40 hours of Job Basis Leave for eligible positions

Tuition Reimbursement (Up to 2K annually)

General Description

Performs professional environmental work enforcing the provisions of environmental ordinances as well as participates in natural resource enhancement and protection efforts.

Works under general supervision, independently developing work methods and sequences.

Minimum Education And Experience Requirements

Requires a Bachelor's degree from an accredited college or university with major coursework in chemistry, geology, biology or environmental science or closely related field.

Requires six (6) months experience in natural resource protection based on area of assignment or closely related experience.

Special Certifications and Licenses

Must possess and maintain a valid Florida Class E drivers license for duration of appointment. (Depending upon area of assignment.)

Preferences

Master's degree in environmental science or related field
PhD degree in environmental science or related field
OSHA Hazwoper Certification
Florida-Certified Pollutant Storage System Contractor (PSSC)
Board-Certified Environmental Scientist
Engineer-in-Training (EIT) Certification
Florida Professional Engineer (PE) License
1 year experience in POSSE/Winchester
1 year experience in design or construction or closure or operation of hazardous materials and/or storage tanks facilities
1 year experience with local or State rules and regulations regarding hazardous materials and/or storage tanks facilities' licensing and/or inspection
Florida Class A, B or C and/or STI/API Tank Training
FDEP Storage Tank Inspector Training
NAHMMA Small Quantity Generator Inspector Training
RCRA Hazardous Waste Training (HAZWOPER)
1 year experience in GIS
1 year experience in Field Sampling and Collection
1 year experience in State or Federal databases (STCM, FIRST, CHAZ, OCULUS, SWIFT, PA, WACS, PMTS, RegDB)
1 year experience with Power BI data analysis and reporting

SCOPE OF WORK

Duties And Responsibilities

The functions listed below are those that represent the majority of the time spent working in this class. Management may assign additional functions related to the type of work of the job as necessary.

The Broward County Board of County Commissioners is seeking qualified candidates for the position of Natural Resources Specialist - inspection concentration with the Pollution Prevention Section of the Environmental Permitting Division. The Pollution Prevention Section regulates, licenses, and inspects hazardous material, storage tank, and wellfield facilities in Broward County to protect the environment, ground and groundwater through applicable environmental regulations within the Broward County Code of Ordinances (the Code) and State and Federal Rules and Regulations.

Natural Resources Specialists with inspection concentration conduct various routine compliance assistance and follow-up hazardous material and/or storage tank facility inspections; cite non-compliance items and issue non-compliance letters; prepare warnings and/or notices of violation and associated correspondence dealing with enforcement of environmental ordinances, rules and regulations; respond to haz-mat and/or storage tank associated Service Requests, citizen complaints, reported spills and discharges; and conduct field sweeps of industrial areas in search of regulated businesses operating without the required haz-mat/storage tank facility licenses. Storage tank facility type inspections also include install, closure, discharge investigation and complaint investigation inspections at State and County regulated facilities in Broward County. Field Inspectors generally input their findings into the inspection databases, and maintain electronic files of documented observations, records reviewed, digital photos taken, test results received, site sketches, etc. and electronically issue associated notices and/or inspection reports to the regulated businesses in Broward County.

This hands-off position is mainly responsible for conducting field inspections at State and/or County regulated haz-mat and storage tank facilities in Broward County, and ensuring compliance with all applicable environmental regulatory requirements. Tasks performed include educating the regulated community regarding the compliance program's purposes, requirements, processes and procedures; communicating with business representatives on-site in person, and/or by phone, email, or other written correspondence on compliance issues; scheduling inspections and follow-up activities; conducting electronic inspections by photo-documenting observations, inputting compliance and non-compliance findings, information into the databases; processing, maintaining and forwarding associated inspection reports electronically; citing non-compliance issues and processing and tracking associated enforcement activities to ultimately ensure compliance with licensing and/or regulatory requirements.

Field Inspectors regularly coordinate internally with each other, Licensing Coordinator Natural Resources Specialists, Senior staff, Technical Support staff, Supervisors and/or Managers, and externally with Contractors, Permittees and/or the Regulated Community representatives regarding the Code and applicable inspections' rules, requirements, processes, procedures and regulations. Natural Resources Specialists in their capacity as Field Inspectors must possess strong customer service skills to coordinate, schedule and conduct field inspection activities, and the ability to communicate effectively and professionally in person, on the phone and in writing. Field Inspectors must also possess knowledge of hazardous material facility and storage tank system operations, strong organizational and computer skills, including the use of workflow databases, the Internet (for research and on-line business info, registration, etc.), MS Suite (Outlook, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Teams, etc.) and Adobe Acrobat. Natural Resources Specialists are required to stay abreast of current applicable environmental technology and EPA, State and local rules and regulations and perform related work as assigned.

Competencies

Tech Savvy: Anticipates and adopts innovations in business-building digital and technology applications. Investigates technologies to learn some cutting-edge best practices. Uses digital/social media to benefit the team and add value to the work being done; understands how to avoid misuse of these tools.
Manages Complexity: Makes sense of complex, high quantity, and sometimes contradictory information to effectively solve problems. Quickly determines the most critical data and focuses analysis there; recognizes even subtle symptoms that indicate problems; probes deeply for root causes; uses systematic problem-solving methods. Well.
Decision Quality: Makes good and timely decisions that keep the organization moving forward. Swiftly internalizes coaching on routine issues; handles issues confidently after instruction. Leverages rules and procedures to speed up decision making. Confidently and quickly draws on others' expertise.
Optimizes Work Processes: Knows the most effective and efficient processes to get things done, with a focus on continuous improvement. Pursues, explores, and develops ways to ensure own work is as effective as possible within all relevant processes. Shares an analysis of process problems with stakeholders; discusses how to resolve the issue.
Ensures Accountability: Holds self and others accountable to meet commitments. Accepts responsibility for own work, both successes and failures. Handles fair share and does not make excuses for problems. Usually meets commitments to others.
Communicates Effectively: Develops and delivers multi-mode communications that convey a clear understanding of the unique needs of different audiences. Seeks out others' perspectives and asks good questions. Shares information that people want to know; gives appropriate context and details when speaking.
Courage: Steps up to address difficult issues, saying what needs to be said. Is known for expressing views directly and respectfully; communicates what needs to be said. Assumes personal ownership and responsibility when confronted or challenged; shows readiness to learn and to resolve issues.

WORK ENVIRONMENT

Physical Demands

Physical demands refer to the requirements for physical exertion and coordination of limb and body movement.

Performs light work that involves walking or standing most of the time and involves exerting up to 20 pounds of force on a regular and recurring basis, or skill, adeptness and speed in the use of fingers, hands or limbs on repetitive operation of mechanical or electronic office equipment or tools within moderate tolerances or limits of accuracy.

Unavoidable Hazards (Work Environment)

Unavoidable hazards refer to the job conditions that may lead to injury or health hazards even though precautions have been taken.

Involves routine and frequent exposure to disease/pathogens. (Depending upon area of assignment.)

About The Company

Hims & Hers is the leading health and wellness platform dedicated to transforming the way individuals access and experience healthcare. With a mission to help the world feel great through better health, the company is committed to providing personalized, accessible, and affordable healthcare solutions. By normalizing health and wellness challenges and fostering innovative approaches to treatment, Hims & Hers aims to make better health outcomes more achievable for everyone. As a public company listed on the NYSE under the ticker symbol “HIMS,” it exemplifies a forward-thinking, customer-centric approach in the digital health space. To learn more about the company's offerings and philosophy, visit hims.com/about and hims.com/how-it-works. The organization also emphasizes a flexible, remote work culture and offers outstanding benefits to its employees, reinforcing its commitment to a supportive and inclusive workplace environment.

About The Role

As a Staff Analyst in Product Analytics at Hims & Hers, you will play a pivotal role in shaping the customer experience through advanced experimental design and hypothesis testing. Your expertise will enable the company to develop data-driven strategies that enhance user engagement and satisfaction. Working closely with cross-functional teams—including product managers, growth leads, designers, and engineers—you will lead efforts to design, execute, and analyze A/B tests and other experiments. Your insights will influence product development roadmaps and strategic decisions, ensuring that features and initiatives are backed by robust data analysis. Reporting directly to the Sr Director of Product Analytics, you will also be responsible for developing dashboards, KPIs, and measurement frameworks that democratize data access and foster a culture of data literacy across the organization. Your role is critical in identifying causal relationships, segmenting users, and providing actionable recommendations that drive business growth and improve health outcomes for users.

Qualifications

8+ years of experience in analytics, data science, or a related quantitative field
Bachelor’s degree in Statistics, Mathematics, Economics, Computer Science, Engineering, or a related discipline
5+ years of experience designing, executing, and analyzing A/B tests in a product environment
Experience working with subscription-based business models and associated metrics
Extensive experience collaborating with data engineering teams and managing production data pipelines
Strong knowledge of data modeling, experimental design, and statistical inference
Expertise in SQL and advanced data visualization tools such as Looker or Tableau
Proficiency in programming languages like Python, SAS, or R
Experience developing and deploying predictive models
Ability to communicate complex technical analyses to non-technical stakeholders, including executives
Proven track record in shaping product strategy through data insights
Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage long-term projects independently

Responsibilities

Provide strategic thought leadership and collaborate with product stakeholders to influence product roadmaps through data-driven insights
Lead the experimentation strategy, including test design, success metrics, sample size estimation, and results interpretation
Define tracking requirements, ensure data integrity, and oversee analytics instrumentation across products
Create intuitive dashboards in Looker to democratize data and enhance data self-service capabilities
Develop and maintain KPI frameworks and measurement plans for new features and initiatives
Champion data quality, documentation, and consistency of deliverables, mentoring junior analysts as needed
Identify causal relationships using advanced statistical modeling, quasi-experimental methods, and predictive analytics
Segment users based on behavioral, demographic, and psychographic data to personalize product experiences and communications
Conduct deep-dive analyses to answer strategic business questions, quantify opportunities, and recommend actionable insights

Benefits

Competitive salary and equity compensation packages
Unlimited paid time off, company holidays, and quarterly mental health days
Comprehensive health benefits including medical, dental, and vision coverage, along with parental leave
Employee Stock Purchase Program (ESPP)
401(k) plan with employer matching contributions
Offsite team retreats and team-building events
Flexible and remote work environment that promotes work-life balance

We consider all qualified applicants regardless of race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, age, disability, or veteran status. We also provide reasonable accommodations for applicants with disabilities or disabled veterans in our hiring process. We believe that a diverse workforce enhances our ability to serve our customers and innovate effectively. new_jobs.title: Agricultural Field Technician
new_jobs.description:
Amalgamated Sugar Company is looking for a Agriculture Field Technician working under the direction of our Chief Scientist – Senior Plant Pathologist, this role is focused on managing the day-to-day operations of the Amalgamated Sugar Company’s insectary and greenhouse (estimated 20-30 hrs./week), as well as supporting scientifically rigorous research trials in the field (estimated 10-20 hrs./week). You will be a part of a team dedicated to contributing new knowledge to sugarbeet growers in Idaho, Oregon, and Washington to enable them to improve their sugarbeet productivity, profitability, and sustainability. The role is ideally suited to someone who has an eye for detail, enjoys working in a greenhouse setting with insects, and has an inquisitive mind. Research conducted includes agronomy and farming system research trials, as well as the evaluation of new pesticides for the control of diseases, insects, and weeds. Based in Nyssa, OR, this position is with Amalgamated Sugar Company’s Sugarbeet Research (SBR) Team.

Primary Responsibilities

Insectary and Greenhouse Management

Manage day-to-day insectary and greenhouse operations with minimal supervision, prioritizing tasks to meet timelines.
Propagate, grow, and maintain sugarbeet plants to support insect colonies and experiments (e.g., seeding, transplanting, watering, fertilization, and sanitation).
Rear beet leafhoppers and maintain healthy colonies; produce and deliver adequate numbers of viruliferous leafhoppers for field trials according to established protocols.
Scout plants routinely for insects, mites, and diseases; implement integrated pest management (IPM) and apply pesticides as needed in accordance with label directions and all applicable state/federal requirements.
Maintain greenhouse and insectary infrastructure, including environmental controls, irrigation systems, lighting, benches, and insect containment features; perform and coordinate repairs and preventive maintenance as needed.
Monitor and document key environmental parameters (e.g., temperature, humidity, and photoperiod) and adjust settings to maintain consistent plant and insect performance.
Maintain cleanliness to prevent spread of pests or pathogens between experiments and growing areas.
Maintain accurate records for pesticide applications, and trial support activities.
Track and maintain inventory of plants, insects, growing supplies, and chemicals; coordinate ordering and proper storage/disposal in compliance with regulations.
Promote safe work practices in the greenhouse and insectary, including proper PPE use, chemical handling, and hazard reporting; recommend and implement improvements to safety procedures.

Field and Technical Support

Support the Chief Scientist – Senior Plant Pathologist and Research Agronomist in planning, organizing, and executing field and glasshouse research trials.
Assist with establishing experiments, including trial design support, plot layout and marking, planting/seeding, and accurate application of experimental treatments.
Perform routine cultural practices and plot maintenance (e.g., cultivation, thinning, fertilization support, replanting, and border management) to maintain trial integrity.
Manage day-to-day trial operations, including irrigation scheduling, crop scouting, and weed/insect/disease control; calibrate and operate application equipment and ensure treatments are applied safely and according to protocol and label requirements.
Collect research measurements and samples as assigned; follow protocols for sampling, labeling, handling, and storage to protect data quality and traceability.
Assist with harvest operations, including plot harvesting and collection of yield and quality data.
Enter, organize, and format trial data using Microsoft Excel; perform basic data checks to identify missing values, outliers, or inconsistencies.
Maintain accurate, timely records of trial activities (e.g., field operations, treatment applications, scouting observations, deviations, and equipment logs) in accordance with research documentation standards.
Assist with transporting research and farm equipment by road, including safe loading/unloading, securing loads, and trailering as needed.
Operate, clean, and perform routine maintenance on research equipment and small plot implements (e.g., planters, sprayers, pumps, and sensors) and report repair needs promptly.
Communicate progress and field observations (e.g., pest pressure, disease symptoms, stand issues, irrigation problems) and escalate urgent issues to project leads in a timely manner.
Coordinate day-to-day logistics for trial work, including staging supplies, preparing labels and datasheets, and assisting with training/oversight of seasonal staff when assigned.
Ensure field and glasshouse work is conducted safely (PPE, chemical safety, equipment operation, and heat/cold stress awareness) and contribute to continuous improvement of safe work practices.

Secondary RESPONSIBILITIES

Administrative Support

Assist with preparation of reports/information for publication and/or presentation to industry.
Assist with the design and development of innovative extension materials.
Assist with the preparation of the Sugarbeet Research Magazine.
Supervision of seasonal field staff as required

Essential Skills And Attributes

Interest in greenhouse work and entomology; comfort working around insects is essential.
Plant production and care skills (seeding, transplanting, watering, fertilization), insect rearing/handling, pesticide use, and operation of basic farm/greenhouse implements.
Valid driver’s license in Idaho or Oregon (or ability to obtain).
Current Idaho and Oregon pesticide applicator license(s), or willingness/ability to obtain both within 6 months of employment.
Idaho or Oregon Commercial Class A driver’s license (CDL), or willingness/ability to obtain within 6 months of employment.
Strong attention to detail and the ability to follow research protocols, treatment plans, and data-collection methods consistently.
Comfortable with accurate recordkeeping and documentation (e.g., pesticide application records, environmental logs, and trial notes).
Basic math and measurement skills for mixing, calibrating, and applying treatments and for collecting field/greenhouse data.
Mechanical aptitude and comfort operating, troubleshooting, and maintaining common greenhouse.
Ability to follow sanitation, containment, and biosecurity procedures to protect insect colonies and prevent cross-contamination between trials.
Proficiency with Microsoft Excel, Word, and PowerPoint; willingness to learn Adobe InDesign.
Highly organized with the ability to plan work, manage multiple projects, and meet deadlines with minimal supervision.
Commitment to workplace safety, including proper PPE, chemical safety, equipment safety, and proactive hazard identification and reporting.
Comfort performing hands-on work in greenhouse and outdoor conditions, including heat, cold, dust, and moisture.
Ability to travel for work, including occasional overnight stays.
Ability to work under time-sensitive conditions while maintaining a professional, steady approach.
High personal integrity, reliability, and a commitment to producing accurate, high-quality work.
Collaborative, team-oriented mindset; communicates effectively and builds positive working relationships internally and externally.

Minimum Education And Experience

A bachelor’s degree with an emphasis in agronomy, soil, or plant science is required.
Experience with greenhouse operations is required and with farm equipment is desirable.
The ability to obtain and maintain a ID/OR pesticide applicator license is required, and to obtain and maintain an Idaho or Oregon State Commercial Class A driver’s license (CDL) is desirable.
Knowledge of trial management or replicated small plot research is desirable
Preferred 2-4 years of work-related experience in the field;
OR any equivalent combination of experience and education which provides the required knowledge, skills, and abilities.

.

Brief Description

Locke Solutions is a premier provider of custom precast concrete solutions and was recently recognized as Houston’s #1 Fastest Growing Company by the Houston Business Journal. We’re in an exciting period of growth and transformation, expanding from one to three locations in just two years, and we’re on track to reach $100 million in revenue by 2027.

Our core values—responsiveness, teamwork, an ownership mentality, a ‘get it done’ attitude, and problem-solving—form the foundation of our inclusive and collaborative culture. We genuinely care about our employees and customers, as enshrined in our stated Purpose: to make customers’ lives easier and employees’ lives better.

Role Summary/Purpose:

The Project Coordinator at Locke Solutions plays a critical support role in assisting Project Managers with the planning, execution, and coordination of precast concrete projects. This position focuses on maintaining accurate ERP (Titan) data, coordinating material procurement, and supporting project schedules to ensure timely and efficient project delivery.

This role requires a highly detail-oriented and proactive individual who can manage multiple tasks, ensure data accuracy, and collaborate effectively across departments. The ideal candidate will help streamline project operations, reduce administrative burden on Project Managers, and contribute to successful project outcomes through strong organization and follow-through.

Key Responsibilities:

Accurately enter, update, and maintain project data in Titan ERP, including BOMs, product details, and cost information.
Coordinate material procurement by working with purchasing teams to ensure timely ordering and delivery of materials.
Track vendor lead times, confirm delivery dates, and proactively follow up on material status.
Assist in developing and maintaining project schedules, including tracking key milestones such as submittals, production, and shipping.
Monitor project timelines and communicate potential delays or risks to Project Managers.
Prepare and manage project documentation, including submittals, RFIs, change orders, and closeout documents.
Maintain and organize all project files within the Titan Document Database, ensuring accuracy and accessibility.
Support internal communication between engineering, production, logistics, and purchasing teams.
Ensure alignment between procurement, production schedules, and delivery commitments.
Assist Project Managers with project setup, kickoff preparation, and ongoing coordination tasks.
Identify opportunities to improve data accuracy, procurement processes, and scheduling efficiency.

Key Results:

Maintain highly accurate ERP data with minimal errors or rework.
Ensure materials are ordered and delivered on time to support project schedules.
Keep project schedules updated and aligned with procurement and production activities.
Reduce Project Manager administrative workload, improving overall team efficiency.
Ensure all project documentation is complete, organized, and accessible throughout the lifecycle.
Support on-time project delivery by proactively identifying and resolving coordination issues.
Maintain strong internal communication and collaboration across departments.

Qualifications:

Associate’s or Bachelor’s degree in Construction Science, Business Administration, or a related field (preferred).
1–4 years of experience in project coordination, construction, manufacturing, or a similar environment.
Experience with ERP systems (Titan or similar preferred).
Strong attention to detail and organizational skills.
Excellent communication and interpersonal abilities.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite, especially Excel.
Ability to multitask and prioritize effectively in a fast-paced environment.
Experience in construction, manufacturing, or precast industry is a plus.

Why Join Locke Solutions?

At Locke Solutions, we are passionate about delivering exceptional customer service and fostering an empowering work environment. We embrace innovation, collaboration, and a commitment to excellence. Join us and be a part of a company that values its employees and is dedicated to making a meaningful impact in our industry.

Job Description

Because of the need for consistent, in-person collaboration and/or the requirement to perform all work onsite due to the nature of this particular role, it will be performed full-time on site. This means work will be conducted on location at a BAE Systems facility 100% of the time.

You don’t see it, but it’s there. Our employees work on the world’s most advanced electronics – from saving emissions in the City of Lights to powering the Mars Rover to protecting the F35 fighter jet. At Electronic Systems, you’ll be among the brightest minds, working on the aerospace and defense industry’s most difficult problems. Drawing strength from our differences, we’re innovating for the future. And you can, too. Our flexible work environment provides you a chance to change the world without giving up your personal life. We put our customers first – exemplified by our missions: “We Protect Those Who Protect Us®” and “We Innovate For Those Who Move The WorldTM.” Sound like a team you want to be a part of? Come build your career with BAE Systems

In Precision Strike & Sensing Solutions, we design and manufacture state-of-the-art systems and technology that enable our customers to execute their precision strike missions.

Join our dynamic team as a Project Coordinator, where you’ll play a vital role in enabling our engineers and programs to succeed. As a highly organized and tech-savvy professional, you’ll provide a wide variety of administrative, documentation, and process support to multiple engineering teams, ensuring seamless project execution. Assignments typically include non-technical documentation support, parts ordering, general inquiry and problem solving, application/tool support, and coordination of program tasks. If you’re a motivated and detail-oriented professional with a passion for supporting high functioning and fast paced teams, we encourage you to apply for this exciting opportunity.

Edit and format engineering documentation. Interfaces with technicians, engineers and engineering managers to create/edit documentation. Verifies change requests are in the proper state and implemented into documentation.

Supports the Bid & Proposal process, assisting in bid narratives and bid reviews.
Administer the engineering change management process, including facilitating stakeholder reviews
Assists in managing classified laboratory needs, including secure data transfers
Acts as primary focal and liaison for program support, across engineering and other departments
Networks with both internal and external personnel at multiple levels in own area of expertise.
Generally works on moderately difficult assignments which are given in terms of objectives to be accomplished and priorities to be followed. Requires judgment in resolving issues or in making recommendations.

Assists the Project Engineers in tracking and/or maintenance of program/project schedules, milestone performance, and financial metrics.
Assists the Project Engineers in managing daily tasking via JIRA or other tools
Coordinates the interaction of project/program team and support functions to communicate schedule and status.
Acts independently to determine methods and procedures on new or special assignments. Often acts as a facilitator and team leader.
Represents organization as a prime contact on projects, coordinating activities of support personnel and communicating effectively.

High school diploma or equivalent and 3 years work experience
Candidate must be a U.S. citizen
Candidate must be able to obtain a DoW Secret security clearance
Experience with customer service or support
Experience reading BOMs
Proficient in MS Office products (Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Visio)

Preferred Education, Experience, & Skills

Detail oriented with ability to prioritize tasks
Strong interpersonal skills
Proven ability to work independently to support multiple teams and tasks
Ability to retain information quickly
Self-starter

Excellent organizational and problem solving skills

Full-Time Salary Range: $66017 - $105628

Please note: This range is based on our market pay structures. However, individual salaries are determined by a variety of factors including, but not limited to: business considerations, local market conditions, and internal equity, as well as candidate qualifications, such as skills, education, and experience.

Employee Benefits: At BAE Systems, we support our employees in all aspects of their life, including their health and financial well-being. Regular employees scheduled to work 20+ hours per week are offered: health, dental, and vision insurance; health savings accounts; a 401(k) savings plan; disability coverage; and life and accident insurance. BAE Systems, Inc. is the U.S. subsidiary of BAE Systems plc, an international defense, aerospace and security company which delivers a full range of products and services for air, land and naval forces, as well as advanced electronics, security, information technology solutions and customer support services. Improving the future and protecting lives is an ambitious mission, but it’s what we do at BAE Systems. Working here means using your passion and ingenuity where it counts – defending national security with breakthrough technology, superior products, and intelligence solutions. As you develop the latest technology and defend national security, you will continually hone your skills on a team—making a big impact on a global scale. At BAE Systems, you’ll find a rewarding career that truly makes a difference. Electronic Systems (ES) is the global innovator behind BAE Systems’ game-changing defense and commercial electronics. Exploiting every electron, we push the limits of what is possible, giving our customers the edge and our employees opportunities to change the world. Our products and capabilities can be found everywhere – from the depths of the ocean to the far reaches of space. At our core are more than 14,000 highly talented Electronic Systems employees with the brightest minds in the industry, we make an impact – for our customers and the communities we serve.

Position Title

Program Coordinator (DISP Court Coordinator)

Job Description

Interviews:
Generally, interviews will be scheduled within two weeks after the application deadline. May take longer, depending on the number of applications.

Who We Are

Oregon Judicial Department (OJD) serves the public, and the people we serve may be facing challenging life circumstances, high levels of stress, or confusion about their next steps. The work you will do in this role affects members of our community who come to the court to have their cases resolved. We need people who want to impact their communities, value OJD’s efforts to remove barriers to access justice services, and welcome interacting with the public.

We are committed to building a diverse, inclusive team and encourage candidates of all backgrounds to apply. We consider relevant work experience, education, and any transferable skills and abilities that may meet our qualifications or the skills and attributes we need for this position. We welcome all candidates who are inspired by our work and mission.

Benefits To You

We pay 95% to 99% of medical insurance premiums for full-time employees [OR up to 99% of medical insurance premiums for part-time employees], including mental health coverage.
The hourly equivalent for this position is $38.69 - $60.02. [OR the annual salary for this position is $80,467 - $124,833.]
10 paid holidays, 2 floating holidays, 3 personal business days, separate sick and vacation paid leaves (prorated for part-time employees), and other employee benefits such as optional insurances and flexible spending plans.
OJD will pay you a 5% allowance for bilingual skills (includes ASL) if you can pass a skills test and are assigned to use those skills on the job!
Salary offers are made with consideration of the candidate’s education and experience.

Location Highlights

Portland, Oregon was founded in 1845 (incorporated in 1851). It is the state’s largest city and the county seat for Multnomah County. It is named for Portland, Maine. It is situated at the confluence of the Willamette and Columbia Rivers. Recreational activities include, numerous museums (including OMSI), parks (including Forest Park, largest wilderness park in city limits in the nation), hiking (including in-city hiking trails), restaurants (including Food Carts), Mt Hood (about 50 miles east) and much more. Portland is home to three major sports teams: Trailblazers (NBA), Timbers (MLS), and Thorns (NWSL).

Position Highlights

The Multnomah County Circuit Court is hiring a DUII Intensive Supervisor Program (DISP) Court Coordinator
(Program Coordinator).

In this role…

You will serve as the primary point of contact between the treatment court team: including the judge, prosecutors, defense counsel, probation officers, treatment providers, case manager, and peer mentors, and judicial staff ensuring integrated communication and cohesive operations.

Lead and manage regular staffing meetings and court sessions, preparing rosters and progress summaries to support informed decision-making.

Engage in evidence-based practices that are in alignment with the Oregon Specialty Court Standards, All Rise Best Practice Standards, and Ten Guiding Principles for DWI Courts.

Assist the team DDA with the screening process for eligible DUII court candidates which includes, providing risk assessments and collecting DUII court screening data for ongoing internal assessment regarding equitable and efficient referral and entry processes. Additionally, you will be involved with the department analyst for ongoing internal data tracking and internal evaluation processes.

Attend all team meetings and court events and use the court case management system (Odyssey) and the Treatment Court Case Management System (TCMS) to schedule the court’s dockets, produce and maintain all documentation related to the operation of the program, enter data reflecting the work of the court, and record case events for all court proceedings. You will gather information related to participant engagement and compliance with program directives through contact with case managers, community partners, or other public or private sector agencies and update Odyssey and TCMS. You will gather and maintain statistics critical to grant reporting and compliance. You will also monitor grant compliance, spending, and submission. You will maintain and update policy/procedure manuals and participant handbooks to ensure clarity and compliance with program standards.

Work collaboratively with the department analyst to conduct programmatic quality assurance, examining the effectiveness of services, and recommending adjustments to case management or treatment options. You will work with the team to ensure application of culturally competent practices and make programmatic adjustments / refinements based on individual participant needs.

Build and maintain strong collaborative partnerships with national and state treatment court training divisions (Impaired Driving Solutions (IDA), OSCA Treatment Court Team, Criminal Justice Commission (DCJ), Department of Community Justice (DCJ) Oregon Department of Transportation (ODOT), and Local Public Safety Council (LPSCC).

Assigned tasks may be changed to accommodate workload and organizational needs.

Application Process

Workday times out after approximately 15 minutes of inactivity and all progress will be lost.
